podcast.body: This song from "The Joshua Tree" album was inspired by Truman Capote's novel "In Cold Blood," which chronicles the true, senseless murder of a Kansas family. Its lyrics were a "motivating factor" for John Bardo, who interpreted parts as references to himself and Rebecca Schaefer, leading him to stalk and murder her. Horrified by this connection, U2 subsequently stopped playing the song live for the next 30 years. "The lyrics apparently were a motivating factor in Bardot's motives. I quote, he interpreted parts of the lyrics as references to himself and Schaeffer. The song inspired him to do what he did. U2 was of course horrified. They didn't play the song live for the next 30 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Track 10 on The Joshua Tree, this song was created on the very last day of the album's sessions from a long jam that was edited down, captured in one take. It lyrically draws from Norman Mailer's "The Executioner Song" (about Gary Gilmore) and Truman Capote's "In Cold Blood," leading Bono to describe the character as a "serial killer, sort of." The song was performed on all 109 of the original Joshua Tree tour shows, but was played only one other time until the 30th anniversary tour. "There's something that happens when YouTube bashes it out in the band room and sometimes things get out of control, sonically, in a good way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
